big: Dadi's neighbour passed away without telling anyone where his accounts were. His family spent two years finding them, and some were never found. The money was there. The map was not.

lines: Why plan for something that happens after I am gone?
Because the people you love will be the ones dealing with it. A little planning now saves them months of work and many arguments later.

rows: Everything a person owns at death
A person entitled by law or by a will to inherit
How assets pass under personal law when there is no valid will
A court document confirming who may claim certain assets
note: Rules depend on a person's religion and personal law. Ask a lawyer about your own case.

title: Why plan
stops: An estate is everything a person owns at death
Without a will, assets pass as the family chooses
A legal heir is entitled by law or by a will
A succession certificate is never needed
caps: Property, savings, investments and belongings all count.
Without a will, personal law decides who inherits, not the family.
A spouse and children are among those entitled by law.
A court may ask for it before releasing some assets, such as bank balances.

q: Rohan dies without a valid will. Who decides how his assets pass?
opts: The bank that holds his savings
The neighbour who knew him best
why: A bank holds assets but does not decide who the heirs are.
A neighbour has no legal role in deciding who inherits.
First come, first served is not the rule for inheritance.
Without a will, the rules of personal law decide who inherits.

q: Meena's father leaves a house, savings and shares. What is the word for all of it together?
why: A premium is a payment for insurance, and not a name for assets.
An estate is everything a person owns at death.
A deductible is the part of an insurance loss that a person pays.
A nominee is a person named to receive an asset, not the assets.

q: A bank asks Meena's family for a document confirming who can claim her late mother's balance. What may that be?
opts: A shop receipt for a purchase
why: A court issues it to confirm who may claim certain assets.
A brochure describes products and has no role here.
A credit report records borrowing, and does not say who the heirs are.
A shop receipt has no link to who may claim the balance.

q: Which step helps a family most in the first months after a death?
opts: Searching for the papers after the funeral
Leaving accounts for others to guess
Knowing where every account and paper is kept
Closing all accounts quickly without records
why: Searching afterwards is the slow, stressful route that planning avoids.
Guessing leaves some assets unclaimed or lost.
A clear list of accounts and papers saves months of searching.
Closing accounts without records can lose assets and cause disputes.

pts: An estate is everything a person owns at death.
Without a valid will, personal law decides who inherits.
A succession certificate may be needed to claim some assets.
